CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left lower back pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with left-sided lower back pain. He reports a history of back surgery in November 2020, which was a microdiscectomy for a herniated disk that had wrapped around the spinal thecal sac, causing severe nerve pain radiating down the leg. Post-operatively, he was treated with high-dose gabapentin, which was difficult to discontinue. Currently, he experiences left-sided lower back pain, generally around the surgical site, though it varies day to day. Pain is exacerbated by bending over and prolonged standing/weightbearing. Pain improves with stretching. He denies current nerve pain down the legs. He has been managing pain with ibuprofen 800 mg daily. He denies trying ice for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies nerve pain down legs. Denies any other acute problems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back surgery (microdiscectomy) November 2020 for herniated disk with compression of spinal thecal sac.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a veteran receiving care at VA. He is married and reports good support from spouse who encourages stretching and physical therapy.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient able to stand and ambulate.
Back: Pain with weightbearing while standing. Pain with palpation to left lower back at L5. No pain with palpation to right side. Surgical site appears healed. Pain not elicited with forward flexion or extension of spine at this time.
Extremities: Dorsiflexion normal bilaterally. Normal strength with foot push-back against resistance. No pain with lower extremity testing.

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures. No acute bony abnormalities. Evidence of prior surgical intervention with appropriate healing.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left lower back pain, likely muscular strain related to spinal misalignment post-microdiscectomy. Initiate physical therapy through VA. Continue stretching.
2. Pain management: Discontinue ibuprofen 800 mg daily. Start meloxicam. Referral to pain management for further discussion regarding pain management strategies and judicious use of narcotics. Prescribed demerol as requested.
